'''Nairi Sedrakyan''' (born 1961 in [[Ninotsminda]], [[USSR]]) is Erdős Award 2022 winner [[Armenian people|Armenian]] [[mathematician]] involved in national and international Olympiads, including American Mathematics Competitions (USA) and [[International_Mathematical_Olympiad|IMO]], having been the president of the Armenian Mathematics Olympiads, the Leader of Armenian [[International Mathematical Olympiad|IMO]] Team,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.imo-official.org/year_reg_team.aspx?year=2012&code=ARM |title=International Mathematical Olympiad |website=Imo-official.org |accessdate=2016-12-18}}</ref> a jury member and problem selection committee member of the [[International Mathematical Olympiad]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://imo-official.org/problems/IMO2010SL.pdf |title=International Mathematical Olympiad : 51st IMO Shortlisted Problems with Solutions |website=Imo-official.org |accessdate=2016-12-18}}</ref> a jury member and problem selection committee member of the Zhautykov International Mathematical Olympiad (IZhO),<ref>{{cite web |url=http://srb.imomath.com/zadaci/2015_zhautykov_resenja_e.pdf |title=XI International Zhautykov Olympiad in Sciences |date=January 2015 |website=Srb.imomath.com |accessdate=2016-12-18 |archive-date=15 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160315130813/http://srb.imomath.com/zadaci/2015_zhautykov_resenja_e.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref> a jury member and problem selection committee member of the International Olympiad of Metropolises,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://srb.imomath.com/zadaci/2016_metropolis_resenja_e.pdf |title=The ist International Olympiad of Metropolises |date=September 2016 |website=Srb.imomath.com |accessdate=2016-12-18 |archive-date=20 December 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161220152246/http://srb.imomath.com/zadaci/2016_metropolis_resenja_e.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref> the president and organizer of the International Mathematical Olympiad [[Tournament of the Towns]] in the Republic of Armenia (1986-2013).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://sedrakyans.com/about-me/|title=About me |website=Sedrakyans.com |accessdate=2021-12-13}} </ref> He has also authored a large number of problems proposed in these Olympiads. The [[government of Armenia]] awarded the author the title of the best teacher of Armenia and he received a special gift from the Prime Minister.<ref name=":0">{{cite web|url=http://physmath.schools.am/phismath/physmath.%20en/physmath%20en/Michocarumner%20%20en_files/michocarum%20%20hobelianakan1-en.htm|title=physmath|website=Physmath.schools.am|accessdate=2016-12-18|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303213548/http://physmath.schools.am/phismath/physmath.%20en/physmath%20en/Michocarumner%20%20en_files/michocarum%20%20hobelianakan1-en.htm|archive-date=3 March 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> Nairi Sedrakyan's son Hayk Sedrakyan is also a professional mathematician and former IMO competitor.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.imo-official.org/participant_r.aspx?id=7234|accessdate=2018-05-20|title=International Mathematical Olympiad}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=198632|accessdate=2018-05-20|title=Hayk Sedrakyan - the Mathematics Genealogy Project}}</ref>

Nairi Sedrakyan is known for [[Sedrakyan's inequality]].<ref>{{cite book|author1=Hayk Sedrakyan|author2=Nairi Sedrakyan|title=Algebraic Inequalities|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=8DNjDwAAQBAJ&pg=PA106|year=2018|publisher=Springer|isbn=978-3-319-77836-5|page=106}}</ref>

Nairi Sedrakyan has authored 14 books and around 70 articles in different countries (USA, Switzerland, South Korea, Russia) on the topic of [[problem solving]] and Olympiad style mathematics.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://sedrakyans.com/books/ |title=Books &#124; Nairi Sedrakyan's official website |website=Sedrakyans.com |date=2012-01-31 |accessdate=2016-12-18}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://sedrakyans.com/my-publications/|title=My Publications |website=Sedrakyans.com |accessdate=2016-12-18}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Nairi Sedrakyan was born in the [[USSR]] in the town of [[Ninotsminda]] in the [[Georgian SSR]]. At the age of 14 years old he left [[Ninotsminda]] for [[Yerevan]], [[Armenian SSR]] to advance his mathematical knowledge and to study mathematics at the [[PhysMath School after A. Shahinyan (Yerevan)]], one of the leading schools in Armenia. He continued his Bachelor, Master and PhD studies at the [[Yerevan State University]] in the faculty of Mathematics and Mechanics, widely regarded by students as one of the toughest faculties in the university.<ref name=":0" />

==Mathematics coaching and Olympiads==
The students of Nairi Sedrakyan have obtained 20 medals (1 gold medal, 4 silver medals, 15 bronze medals, one of which was received by his son Hayk Sedrakyan) in the [[International Mathematical Olympiad]], providing more than half of the medals that Armenia received in the history of its participation in the [[International Mathematical Olympiad]]. So far it is the single Gold Medal of Armenia in the [[International Mathematical Olympiad]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.imo-official.org/country_hall.aspx?code=ARM |title=International Mathematical Olympiad |website=Imo-official.org |accessdate=2016-12-18}}</ref>

==Honours==
'''Awards'''
* '''Erdos Award 2022''' http://www.wfnmc.org/awards.html <ref name=":0" /> 
* Gold medal for contributions in the World's Olympic and scientific activities in mathematics. University of Riga and [[Latvian Mathematical Society|Latvian mathematical society]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://sedrakyans.com/39-2/ |title=Awards &#124; Nairi Sedrakyan's official website |website=Sedrakyans.com |date=2012-01-31 |accessdate=2016-12-18}}</ref>
* The highest award of the Ministry of Education and Sciences of Armenia. Gold medal for Olympic activities in mathematics.<ref name=":0" />
* The best teacher of Armenia, 2000. Award of the Ministry of Education and Sciences of Armenia.<ref name=":0" />
* The best teacher of Armenia, 1993. Award of the Ministry of Education and Sciences of Armenia.<ref name=":0" />
* Special gift from the Prime Minister and the government of Armenia, 2000.<ref name=":0" />
